questions.stem: What is the polite masu form of the verb みる, meaning "see"?

options.misconception: uses the plain past form instead of the polite masu (nonpast) of みる
uses the plain negative form instead of the polite masu (nonpast) of みる
uses the te form form instead of the polite masu (nonpast) of みる

questions.explanation: The verb みる, meaning "see", has the polite masu (nonpast) form みます. Japanese verbs change their ending for politeness, negation, past tense, and the te form, and the pattern depends on whether a verb is godan, ichidan, or irregular.
questions.hint: Start from the dictionary form みる and apply the polite masu (nonpast) pattern.
